title: SOP from a task list
prompt: Act as a technical writer. Write a step-by-step SOP for [task] on [system], for [audience]. Use the steps below, in order, one numbered step per action. Add a 'Before you start' section listing [prerequisites] and a 'If it fails' section with [fallback]. Steps: [step 1; step 2; step 3]
sample_context: task=password reset; system=Sample Portal; audience=new helpdesk staff
check_notes: Every step runs in the order written; fallback step is real.

title: Runbook from an outage log
prompt: Act as an IT operations writer. Draft a runbook for [incident type] on [system]. Include: symptoms, first checks, escalation trigger, and recovery steps. Base it only on this log excerpt: [log excerpt]. Do not invent causes that are not in the log.
check_notes: Symptoms match the real incident; nothing invented from the log.

title: Ticket thread to KB article
prompt: Act as a support writer. Turn this resolved ticket thread into a knowledge-base article for [audience]. Structure: problem, cause in one sentence, fix in numbered steps, 'still stuck?' line. Keep it under [word count] words. Ticket thread: [thread summary]
check_notes: The fix was the one that resolved the ticket; no user names remain.

title: Change list to release notes
prompt: Act as a release-notes writer. Summarise these changes for [audience] in plain language: [change 1; change 2; change 3]. Group them under 'New', 'Fixed', and 'Changed'. Leave out anything internal-only.
check_notes: Every item shipped in this release; internal-only items removed.

title: Pre-change checklist
prompt: Act as a change manager. Build a pre-change checklist for [change] on [system]. Include: backup taken, rollback plan, who to notify, and a test step after the change. Output as a tick-box list.
check_notes: Rollback plan is tested, not just written.

title: SOP from a screen recording
prompt: Act as a technical writer. Watch this screen recording of [task] on [system] and write an SOP for [audience]. List every click and field in order. Flag any step you cannot see clearly instead of guessing it.
check_notes: No step is guessed; unclear steps are flagged, not invented.
